claims.text: Friction stir processing with in situ CoCrFeNiMo HEA powder addition produces a refined surface layer on austenitic stainless steel.
The intervention produces a recrystallized surface layer.
The intervention produces a uniform dispersion of HEA particles in the processed layer.
Austenitic stainless steel surfaces containing damage, microstructural defects, and stress concentrations are predisposed to hot cracking.
FSP can be performed without melting the austenitic stainless steel substrate.
Processing below 0.5Tm at approximately 300–600 rpm can produce dynamic recrystallization without melting.
An inert atmosphere and controlled traverse speed help ensure the intended recrystallization and non-melting processing regime.
The processed layer has modified grain boundaries.
The processed layer has reduced residual-stress concentrations.
Severe plastic deformation during FSP triggers dynamic recrystallization.
FSP facilitates in situ mechanical alloying of the added HEA particles.
Solid-state FSP eliminates localized hot zones that can nucleate cracks.
The FSP-treated surface has greater hardness than both fusion-welded repairs and untreated surfaces.
The FSP-treated surface has a lower incidence of hot cracking than both fusion-welded repairs and untreated surfaces.
The FSP-treated surface has greater wear resistance than both fusion-welded repairs and untreated surfaces.
The FSP-treated surface has greater corrosion resistance than both fusion-welded repairs and untreated surfaces in aggressive service environments.
The intervention is applicable to high-value components whose damage is confined to the surface.
Powder particle-size distribution and stirring parameters determine whether a uniform HEA dispersion is achieved.
